content.title: About
content.content: Sloe gin fizz is a classic cocktail made with gin, sloe berries, lemon juice and sparkling water. It is refreshing, lightly sweet‑tart, with a distinctive berry‑forward aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The drink first appeared in the early 1920s in the United Kingdom.
Sloe berries are macerated in gin for several weeks to create sloe gin.
It is traditionally served in a highball glass over ice.
Fresh lemon juice is used in the original recipe, though lime is sometimes substituted.
The cocktail is popular in summer because of its light carbonation.

items.title: Low calorie content
items.content: When consumed in moderation, the cocktail contains fewer calories than many sweet mixed drinks.

items.title: Vitamin C from lemon
items.content: Lemon juice provides vitamin C, which supports the immune system.

items.title: Antioxidants from sloe berries
items.content: Sloe berries are rich in anthocyanins, which have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Alcohol
items.content: The drink contains alcohol and should be consumed responsibly; avoid during pregnancy, driving, or by children.

items.title: Gin allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be sensitive to gin or to sloe berries.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Lemon juice increases acidity and may irritate the stomach of people with gastritis.

content.title: How to Make
content.content: Combine 45 ml sloe gin, 15 ml fresh lemon juice and 10 ml simple syrup in a shaker with ice. Shake well, strain into a highball glass over fresh ice and top with sparkling water. Garnish with a lemon wedge or a sloe berry.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Sloe gin should be stored in a cool, dark place, tightly sealed, for up to 2 years. Sloe berries keep best in the refrigerator in an airtight container, and the finished cocktail should be enjoyed immediately to retain its fizz.
